This improves the previous work of Baker, who obtained the exponent $1/3-2/(3C)+o(1)$ in the case of $y\geq (\log n)^C$, and that of Yau, who obtained the exponent $1/3$ when $y=n^{o(1)}$. Our proof is based on the dispersion method together with arithmetic inputs coming from the average bounds for Kloosterman sums over smooth numbers.
